name: LinguaGapAtlas
title: LinguaGapAtlas: A Corpus and Taxonomy of 96 Multilingual AI Benchmarks and Datasets
description: Machine-readable release of the LinguaGapAtlas corpus: 96 multilingual AI resources (58 benchmarks and 38 datasets under the five-round majority consensus; first released 2005-2025) classified on five taxonomy dimensions (data origin, linguistic resource tier, task class, cultural specificity, inference paradigm). For every resource it gives the consensus labels (null = undetermined), the votes of the five independent coding rounds behind each consensus cell, and each round's own labels, evidence notes, sources and confidence; plus the taxonomy and controlled vocabularies, statistics computed from the labels, and caveats to read before use. The screening log holds 0 candidate rows. The codebook and scripts are in the source repository.

null_rule: null means undetermined: the value could not be determined from the resource's public documentation (or, for a consensus label, the rounds did not reach a majority). Undetermined values are never imputed; exclude them from a statistic's denominator and report their count.

fields.description: Stable ID assigned by this project, form QG-001…QG-096. Never reused, never renumbered between versions.

Full citation (authors, title, venue, year) of the paper or release that introduces the resource. null if the resource has no citable paper.

Benchmark or Dataset. Benchmarks are resources designed for evaluation; datasets are resources designed primarily for training. A resource released as both is coded by its primary stated purpose and the dual nature is noted in evidence_note.
Year of first public release (paper or public artifact, whichever came first). null if not determinable.
Semicolon-separated list of language names (or ISO 639 codes) the resource covers, as documented by its creators. null if the documentation does not enumerate them.
Derived from `languages`: the entries that name a language, in source order (entries such as '75 languages' that only state a count are left out). null when `languages` is null.
true when `language_names` names every covered language: no count-only entries and as many names as `language_count`.
Number of languages covered, counted from languages where enumerated, otherwise the count stated by the creators. null if neither is available. Never estimated.

How the resource's content was produced. Native: authored originally in the target language(s). Translated: produced by translating content from another language (human or machine). Mixed: both routes used for substantial portions. null if the production route is not documented.

Linguistic resource tier of the language(s) the resource targets, per the paper's tiering of language resourcedness. For multilingual resources, the tier of the lowest-resourced language substantially covered. null if the covered languages cannot be established.

The task family the resource evaluates or supports. Benchmarks: QA, Syntax, Reasoning, Multimodal, NLU, Summarization, Math, RAG, Code, Other. Datasets: Pre-training, Translation, Instruction. A resource spanning several classes is coded by its primary class; secondary classes go in evidence_note.

Universal: designed to be culturally non-specific. Culturally Anchored: content is grounded in the cultural context of its language community without being tied to one sub-region. Region-Specific: content is grounded in a particular country/region's context. null if the documentation does not support a judgement.

The inference/evaluation paradigm the resource is built around. Vocabulary to be confirmed against the final codebook before v1.0.0; rows coded before confirmation carry the coder's best judgement and are flagged in confidence. null if not determinable.

The evidence source the row's labels were taken from — the resource's paper, repository, or documentation page actually consulted. Every coded dimension in the row must be supported by this source or by evidence_note. null only for rows with no coded dimensions.
Free-text note recording what the source states that supports the labels (quoted or paraphrased), plus any dual-nature or secondary-class remarks. This is the audit trail for the row.
Always 'consensus-5rounds': the row is the majority vote of the five coding rounds. Each round's coder is its round letter (see rounds).

Derived from the vote, not recorded by a coder: high when none of the voted label cells is split or without majority, medium for 1-2 such cells, low for 3 or more. Each round's own confidence is under rounds.

Disposition of this resource in the screening pipeline (see data/screening-log.csv): for rows in corpus.csv this is always included; the full candidate set, including exclusions, lives in the screening log.
For included rows, the eligibility basis (e.g. which inclusion criterion the resource met). Exclusion reasons are recorded in the screening log, not here.

Per label field, how the five rounds voted: the consensus value, its status (consensus | no_majority | not_coded), the supporting vote count, the number of rounds that coded the cell, whether the rounds split, and every vote with the rounds that cast it.
The five independent coding rounds' own records for this resource (A-E), with labels in canonical form and as written.

dimensions.name: Data Origin
dimensions.definition: How the resource's content was produced. Native: authored originally in the target language(s). Translated: produced by translating content from another language (human or machine). Mixed: both routes used for substantial portions. null if the production route is not documented.

dimensions.name: Linguistic Resource Tier
dimensions.definition: Linguistic resource tier of the language(s) the resource targets, per the paper's tiering of language resourcedness. For multilingual resources, the tier of the lowest-resourced language substantially covered. null if the covered languages cannot be established.

dimensions.name: Task Class
dimensions.definition: The task family the resource evaluates or supports. Benchmarks: QA, Syntax, Reasoning, Multimodal, NLU, Summarization, Math, RAG, Code, Other. Datasets: Pre-training, Translation, Instruction. A resource spanning several classes is coded by its primary class; secondary classes go in evidence_note.

dimensions.name: Cultural Specificity
dimensions.definition: Universal: designed to be culturally non-specific. Culturally Anchored: content is grounded in the cultural context of its language community without being tied to one sub-region. Region-Specific: content is grounded in a particular country/region's context. null if the documentation does not support a judgement.

dimensions.name: Inference Paradigm
dimensions.definition: The inference/evaluation paradigm the resource is built around. Vocabulary to be confirmed against the final codebook before v1.0.0; rows coded before confirmation carry the coder's best judgement and are flagged in confidence. null if not determinable.

coding.design: Five independent blind coding rounds (A-E), each coding all 96 resources from primary sources under the same codebook (rounds-summary.md).

consensus_rules.labels: type, data_origin, resource_tier, task_class and cultural_specificity take a value only when at least 3 of the 5 rounds agree on it after normalization; otherwise the cell is null. inference_paradigm is not voted on: it is round A's cell (every round left it undetermined).
consensus_rules.year: A year reported by at least 2 rounds (on a tie, the one reported first in round order A-E); otherwise round A's cell.
consensus_rules.language_count: The most frequently reported count; on a tie, element n//2 of all n reported counts in ascending order (the upper median); round A's cell when no round reports a count.
consensus_rules.languages: Among the rounds that reported the chosen count, the longest languages text by characters (earliest round on ties), which can be a count statement such as '24 languages'; round A's cell when none of them has one.
consensus_rules.confidence: high when none of the five voted label cells is split or without majority, medium for 1-2 such cells, low for 3 or more.
consensus_rules.scaffold: resource_name, canonical_reference, provenance_url, the screening fields, inference_paradigm and the evidence quoted in evidence_note are round A's (the base round).

coding.reconstruction: Each source CSV has source_columns in this order. corpus.csv is the resource-level fields; a round file is that round's records, with labels taken from labels_as_written, resource_id, resource_name and screening_status from the resource, and coder equal to the round letter. Write null as an empty cell.

statistics.note: Computed from this release's labels; shares exclude undetermined rows from the denominator (scripts/recompute.py). headline_shares groups resources by their consensus type; headline_shares_by_round groups each round's rows by that round's own type label (type_basis 'round'), as recompute.py does when run on a round file. Agreement is Cohen's kappa over the 10 round pairs on normalized labels, counting only resources both rounds coded; the means are over the unrounded pairwise values.

caveats.text: rounds-summary.md states: "The second coders are AI agents; the paper must disclose this as AI second-coding / human–AI agreement, not two-human IAA." This package does not record which rounds were coded by whom.

The consensus corpus has 58 benchmarks and 38 datasets; the paper describes 65 and 31. Shares computed from this release for benchmarks (translated 52.0%, Universal 79.6%, Low tier 100.0% of tier-coded rows) are not the published 26.2%, 55.4% and 6.2% (see rounds-summary.md), and first-release years run 2005-2025, not 2018-2025. Figures in this release are computed from the released labels.

resource_tier has a consensus value for 12 of 96 resources (12 Low; no other tier); 4 more were coded by only 1-2 rounds (no majority) and 80 were left undetermined by every round, because sources rarely state a tier. The low-resource share is not estimable from this release, and tier agreement (kappa 1.0 on a handful of jointly coded pairs) is not a reliability estimate.

inference_paradigm (D5) is null for every resource in the consensus and in every round: the codebook does not enumerate its values (methods/codebook-draft.md, D5), and the vocabulary listed in data-dictionary.md is provisional.

data/screening-log.csv contains 0 candidate rows: the 142-candidate screening record (46 exclusions) that data-dictionary.md describes is not in this release. An empty candidate list is not evidence that no candidates were excluded.

task_class values Generation, Long Context, Embeddings occur in the data but are not in data-dictionary.md's listed vocabulary (they belong to the 13-class set in methods/codebook-draft.md, ambiguity A6). data-dictionary.md lists task classes separately for benchmarks and datasets (applies_to), yet 6 resources carry a class listed only for the other type (QG-038, QG-039, QG-040, QG-048, QG-053, QG-062; codebook ambiguity A9).

At resource level, canonical_reference, provenance_url, screening_reason and the evidence quoted in evidence_note are round A's (the consensus build's base round). In 16 resources round A coded a different value from the consensus for at least one voted label, so the quoted evidence can support a label other than the consensus one. screening_reason is null at resource level because round A left it empty; other rounds record one for 64 resources. Every round's own reference, URL, evidence note, confidence and screening reason is under rounds.
Resource-level confidence is derived from the vote (high: no split or no-majority voted cell; medium: 1-2; low: 3 or more), not recorded by a coder. Each round's own confidence is under rounds.

21 resources document their languages only partly or only as a count (e.g. '75 languages'); for these, language_names holds just the languages actually named and languages_fully_named is false. A further 6 have no documented language list (languages and language_names are null). language_count is as documented, so a value such as 250 for '250+ languages' is a lower bound.
The codebook (methods/codebook-draft.md) is a draft. Adjudication of the split cells and the decision rules it is meant to produce are pending (methods/iaa-protocol.md).
